title: Fishy Business
description: Code for my PhD thesis: transformers, mixture-of-experts and contrastive learning for species, body part, contamination and batch classification from REIMS spectra.

title: Joint Align
description: A Python package for joint retention-time alignment of GC-MS chromatograms across many batches: match peaks by compound, fit one monotone time warp per batch and bring every run into a shared time frame. Plugs into align-bench, with a neural variant in PyTorch.

title: Chroma DCNN
description: Identifying Snapper, Gurnard, Tarakihi and Blue Cod from GC-MS lipid profiles with a 1D dilated CNN, pretrained without labels on MoNA and MassBank reference spectra.

title: Ruru
description: A local, plain-text literature library. Papers arrive from arXiv, OpenAlex, Crossref and journal feeds, get triaged like email, live as Markdown in git and flow into each paper's .bib. Agents use the same CLI I do.

title: GPU Spooler
description: Queue GPU jobs from your laptop onto SSH-reachable servers. A daemon finds free GPUs, runs jobs detached and streams the logs back. Set up out of the box for the VUW ECS cluster.

title: Taura
description: A plain-text provenance ledger that links every number, table and figure in a paper back through a checked chain: artifact, result, run, then commit, config and data version. A convention, a CLI and agent rules, not an experiment tracker.

title: qsh
description: A local-first, privacy-focused CLI that brings vision and semantic understanding to the Unix pipe, powered by a 0.8B Qwen model and Rust.

title: Cloudy with a Chance of Git Pulls
description: A GitHub Action that writes the local weather forecast into a README every 30 minutes, between hidden markers so nothing else is touched. Written up on HackerNoon.

title: ZeroSlop
description: A Chrome extension that flags AI-generated and engagement-farmed posts on X, with local heuristics for extraction hooks and a reporting workflow for bot networks.

title: Teaching Sand to Dream
description: Website for my book on how humans taught sand to dream, from Alan Turing to ChatGPT, told without equations for curious non-experts.
